paragraphs.tag: S01 | gulf wide from altitude, late light: the British fleet as SEPARATE ships spread across the sea (never one column) sailing toward the coast; WASHINGTON BURNED small caption on "burned Washington"; NEW ORLEANS label on its word; the Mississippi glows as one line from the mouth up into the West on "whole American West"; a small seal/ledger icon on "peace table"
paragraphs.text: In the winter of eighteen fourteen, British troops who had burned Washington sailed to take New Orleans, and with it the mouth of the Mississippi, a prize to bargain with at the peace table.

paragraphs.tag: S01 | cloud dive 1 down onto the plain below the city: emerge over the river, the plantations, the cypress swamp; red line-blocks in long lines on the open fields facing a thin brown ditch line; date plate 8 JANUARY 1815 on its words
paragraphs.text: On the eighth of January, eighteen fifteen, more than five thousand British regulars attacked a ditch and a wall of mud below the city.

paragraphs.tag: S01 | the red lines advance; the whole American line flashes with muzzle fire (each shot with its sound), cannon smoke; red blocks break and fall back; number card 2,000+ BRITISH on its words, ticks; then 71 AMERICAN CASUALTIES under it
paragraphs.text: In about half an hour, more than two thousand of them were killed, wounded or captured. The Americans lost seventy-one, killed, wounded or missing.

paragraphs.tag: S01 | hard cut, dark parchment overlay: two wax seals, GHENT on its word; stamp SIGNED on "signed"; caption NOT YET APPROVED on its words
paragraphs.text: And the strangest part? Two weeks earlier, in Ghent, both sides had signed a peace treaty. America had not yet ratified it, so the war went on, and no one in New Orleans knew.

paragraphs.tag: S01 | back to the plain: date plate 23 DECEMBER 1814; red blocks walk out of the cypress swamp onto the river fields; the city label far up the river; distance ruler 9 MILES on its words
paragraphs.text: Two weeks before, a British army had come out of the swamps unseen, nine miles from the city.

paragraphs.tag: S01 | the general enters: banner with no portrait yet riding down into the city; a dark card on "sword": a thin red scar line drawn across it, AGE 14 and BY HIS OWN ACCOUNT small
paragraphs.text: The general sent to save it was worn down by illness, and he carried a scar from a British officer's sword, from when he was fourteen.

paragraphs.tag: S01 | NAME SLAM: ANDREW JACKSON (gold 3D title on its words), the banner portrait revealed; then 3 snap cuts, each on its words: Horseshoe Bend from above (river bend + wall), the night attack (muzzle flashes in the dark, the schooner firing), the mud line with smoke
paragraphs.text: His name was Andrew Jackson. He would trap an enemy fortress inside a river bend. He would attack a British army in the dark, on the night it landed. And he would stop a veteran British army behind a wall of mud. These are Andrew Jackson's three greatest tactical moves.
